# Spec: issue 2, splitting a damage charge loses a cent

## Outcome

When a damage charge does not divide evenly between borrowers, every penny is still billed to someone.
Splitting £33.33 (3333 cents) two ways gives £16.67 and £16.66, which add up to £33.33.

## Requirements

- The system shall return shares that add up to exactly the charge in cents.
- When the charge does not divide evenly, the system shall give the leftover cents to the first borrowers, one cent each, so 3333 split 2 ways is [1667, 1666].
- The system shall keep every share within one cent of every other share.
- When the charge divides evenly, the system shall give every borrower the same share.
- If the charge is not a whole number of cents or is negative, then the system shall refuse it with an error.
- If the number of ways is not a whole number or is less than 1, then the system shall refuse it with an error.

## Must not change

- Amounts stay integer cents; no floats.
- `splitCharge(totalCents, ways)` keeps its name, arguments and return type (an array of `ways` numbers).
- Existing tests in `tests/fees/split.test.ts` keep passing.
- Nothing under `src/auth/` changes.

## Out of scope

- Splitting in proportion to anything other than equal shares.
- Late fees (`src/fees/late.ts`) and the desk command's output format.
- Any change to the tests that already exist.

## Done when

- The new tests in `tests/fees/split.test.ts` pass.
- `bun run gate` exits 0.
